title: Our fixed-parameter latent-moment identification calculation for the Chapter2 heteroscedastic Gaussian hierarchy
proposal_origin: Parent analyst proposed the inversion; delegated analyst independently checked the source hierarchy, moment derivation, inversion and boundary conditions.
status: Ordinary proof and13exact checks complete; independent review pending. Additive restricted analytical progress, not full observed-response identification or numerical replication.

relation_to_source_claims.scope: Checks and extends algebra of the source latent construction. The source empirical recovery, unbiasedness and power claims are not adjudicated by this result. The latent-moment identification proposition is our derived consequence, not presented as a quotation or a new source claim.

parameter_domain: All calculations condition on one finite fixed parameter vector (mu,va,vc,beta0,beta), with va>0,vc>=0,ve=exp(beta0)>0. Source inverse-gamma priors place va,vc in the strictly positive interior; allowing vc=0 is a harmless extension, not a different prior. No averaging over parameter priors is used.

source_faithful_representation.notation: Source C_i has mean mu. Write centered C=C_i-mu ~N(0,vc); this centered variable is independent of genetic innovations. Let Z1,Z2 be independent standard normals independent of all genetic/common effects.
source_faithful_representation.genetics: For MZ, A1=A2~N(0,va). For DZ, A_t=G+H_t with G,H1,H2 mutually independent N(0,va/2). Thus each A_t~N(0,va) and Cov(A1,A2)=rho*va, rho=1 or1/2. Independence of common effect and Gaussian innovations follows the source conditional hierarchy.
source_faithful_representation.trait: Theta_t=mu+A_t+C+sqrt(ve*exp(beta*A_t))*Z_t. This expresses Eqs2.7–2.8 and2.14–2.15, with ve=exp(beta0), beta=beta1. Within MZ pairs the residual variance factor is shared, but residual draws remain conditionally independent.
source_faithful_representation.conditions: Same fixed parameters across both zygosity populations, known genetic correlations1 and1/2, independent residual innovations and centered common effects as above. Both populations must be available. This is not a Gaussian marginal trait assumption when beta is nonzero.

theorem: The map from this fixed parameter vector to the latent-population moments (mean mu, marginal variance T, MZ covariance K_MZ, DZ covariance K_DZ, marginal third central moment m3) is globally injective on the stated domain. Therefore equality of the two latent twin population distributions implies equality of the parameter vector. Finite Rasch item-response probabilities have not been shown to identify these latent moments.

ordinary_proof.name: Absolute moments exist at fixed finite parameters
ordinary_proof.argument: For any positive integer k, the Gaussian A+C has finite absolute kth moment. Independence of Z and A gives E|sqrt(ve exp(beta A))*Z|^k=ve^(k/2) E exp(k beta A/2) E|Z|^k, finite since the centered Gaussian mgf equals exp(va t^2/2) for every finite real t. The inequality |x+y|^k<=2^(k-1)(|x|^k+|y|^k) proves finite absolute central trait moments. Cross-products are integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz. Thus conditional expectation and the cubic expansion below are legitimate. This does not assert existence of the trait mgf at nonzero arguments.

ordinary_proof.name: Mean and twin covariance
ordinary_proof.argument: Given A1,A2,C, each residual has mean zero, so ETheta_t=mu. Its conditional cross residual product expectation is zero because Z1 and Z2 are independent and centered, including the shared-scale MZ case. Residual–genetic/common cross terms also vanish. Therefore K_MZ=va+vc and K_DZ=va/2+vc. Shared random residual scale may induce higher-order dependence; it does not add second cross covariance.

ordinary_proof.name: Marginal variance
ordinary_proof.argument: Write X=A+C and H=sqrt(ve exp(beta A)). Conditional residual variance is H^2 and conditional mean is mu+X. Total variance gives T=va+vc+ve E exp(beta A)=va+vc+ve exp(beta^2 va/2). Define R=T-va-vc=ve exp(beta^2 va/2)>0. In particular ve is environmental variance at A=0; the population residual contribution is R, which generally differs from ve.

ordinary_proof.name: Third central moment
ordinary_proof.argument: Condition on A,C and use EZ=EZ^3=0,EZ^2=1: E[(Theta-mu)^3|A,C]=(A+C)^3+3(A+C)ve exp(beta A). The centered Gaussian A+C has zero third moment. Since C is independent of A and centered, E[C exp(beta A)]=0. Differentiating the Gaussian mgf yields E[A exp(beta A)]=va beta exp(beta^2 va/2). Differentiation is justified, for example, by completing the square and integrability of |A| exp(tA) uniformly for t in a compact neighborhood of beta. Consequently m3=3 va beta ve exp(beta^2 va/2)=3 va beta R.

ordinary_proof.name: Explicit inverse and global latent identification
ordinary_proof.argument: Recover va=2(K_MZ-K_DZ), vc=2*K_DZ-K_MZ, and R=T-va-vc. Because va,R>0, recover beta=m3/(3 va R), then ve=R exp(-beta^2 va/2)>0 and beta0=log(R)-beta^2 va/2. The mean recovers mu directly. Every step is single valued. Thus equal specified latent moments imply equal parameters; no local Jacobian or parameter-count argument is being substituted for global injectivity.

ordinary_proof.name: Sign and zero-interaction limits
ordinary_proof.argument: Because3 va R>0, m3 and beta have the same sign and m3=0 iff beta=0 within the stated domain. When beta=0 the trait pair is jointly Gaussian, R=ve and m3=0. When beta is nonzero the nonzero finite third central moment proves the marginal trait is not Gaussian. Thus the earlier Gaussian item-identification lemma cannot be applied in that case.

boundaries_and_limits.finding: A=0 almost surely, so exp(beta A)=1 for every beta. Beta is unidentifiable and the inverse divides by zero. Excluded; no claim of stable estimation as va approaches zero.
The interaction disappears; outside the finite beta0 domain. R must be positive.
Formulas remain valid for this fixed-parameter boundary, with genetic/common construction interpreted using degenerate C. Source prior remains strictly positive.

boundaries_and_limits.case: Only one zygosity or unequal components across zygosity
boundaries_and_limits.finding: The two-covariance inversion is not justified; no identification theorem for that altered design is asserted.

Not evaluated. Source InvGamma(1,1) for va and vc has infinite mean, so finite fixed-parameter moments do not justify a finite prior-predictive variance or third moment. No exchange of averaging over those priors occurs.

boundaries_and_limits.case: Observed finite binary or ordinal responses
boundaries_and_limits.finding: No proof supplied that their finitely many response-pattern probabilities identify T,K_MZ,K_DZ,m3 in this nonGaussian family. The earlier Gaussian joint-item lemma is inapplicable when beta is nonzero. Ordinal links and unknown item calibration need separate analysis.

Latent-moment inversion refers to a specified trait coordinate. Unknown item difficulties/scale can introduce observational invariances; this proof does not remove them. Source fixes mean when estimating difficulties.
Population inverse neither implies sample unbiasedness, good conditioning, general finite MLE existence/uniqueness, posterior convergence, empirical recovery, effect significance or power.

checks.method: Exact SymPy algebra, including Gaussian-mgf derivative, conditional cubic/cross residual expansions, complete inverse substitution, boundary limits and positive/negative/zero beta examples. Ordinary probabilistic arguments justify the conditional moments; tests do not replace that proof.
checks.Lean: Not performed; ordinary proof only, no formal certification claim.

remaining: Prove or disprove global identification of this nonGaussian parametric latent family from the specified finite calibrated Rasch response law; latent moments being identified by latent distributions is not the missing bridge.
General sample likelihood uniqueness/existence and empirical bias/power are separate unresolved questions.
Independent review required before scientific integration; no inventory, manuscript or baseline changes made.
